destination.name: Lightning Ridge
destination.tagline: An opal-mining town where free artesian pools and underground mine tours are the draw.
destination.description: Lightning Ridge is an outback town and a centre of black opal mining, with a first shaft dug in 1905. Tourism is now as big an industry as mining, with galleries and jewellery shops along the main street. Visitors soak in the Bore Baths, which draw warm water from about 900 m underground, tour the opal tunnels and see a house built of bottles. Wikivoyage warns that it can be very hot in summertime.
whyVisit: Soak in the free Bore Baths
Walk through an underground opal tunnel

goodToKnow.title: Easter books out
goodToKnow.detail: The Easter festival and races fill hotels, and Wikivoyage advises booking around a year ahead.

goodToKnow.title: No public transport
goodToKnow.detail: The town has no public transport and no taxi service, though the Bowling Club runs a transfer service and many hotels help with pickups.

goodToKnow.title: Summer heat
goodToKnow.detail: Wikivoyage warns of exposure in the heat of summer, and the Bore Baths are open around the clock, so go early or late in the day.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Wikivoyage warns of exposure in the summer heat, so {months} are the comfortable months for fossicking and mine tours.
